A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MARC work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. v1 ends after its references despite citing appendices; v2 supplies Appendices A–C. This addition can be compared reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original six-benchmark evaluations, SFT/VMR and threshold ablations, and GPU-memory and latency measurements in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and additionally tabulates benchmark token counts in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The method text and objectives remain unchanged, but v2 Figure 1 adds VMR to the uncompressed branch that bypassed retrieval in v1 Figure 1. Both versions already describe VMR preprocessing of training data. The PDFs do not resolve whether this corrects the schematic or changes teacher inputs.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six evaluation benchmarks and Video-R1 training sources. Appendix B names constituent datasets within the existing training mixture; it does not establish expanded data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 is identical, including the model baselines, ByteVideoLLM, MovieChat, VidCom and SFT variants. Appendix A.2 documents implementations of existing comparators.

E3.justification: Previously specified sampling, frame budgets, model configurations and training sample counts remain unchanged. The appendices disclose additional prompts, resolution limits and optimization settings without reporting revisions to existing protocols. The 16-frame condition already appeared in v1 Table 1.

E4.justification: Tables 2–3 retain identical SFT/VMR comparisons and threshold ablations. Appendix A.4 explains failures using existing results; it provides no separately documented new robustness test, parameter sweep or case-level experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added appendices introduce no statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports the previously unreported 16-frame token-count breakdown, with mean 858.53, and tabulates the 64-frame and compressed counts already represented in v1's plot. Accuracy entries in Tables 1–3 and the efficiency measurements are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain the same token definitions, merging rules, retention reward, advantage normalization and optimization objective. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears in the appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and principal claims: retrieval plus C-GRPO preserves approximately baseline mean accuracy with about 95% fewer visual tokens and reduced memory and latency.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 expands the existing acknowledgment of VideoMME degradation into a specific explanation: top-3 retrieval can discard essential temporal information in long videos that distillation cannot recover. It qualifies applicability by video duration and proposes a temporal Q-Former as future mitigation.

D1.justification: v2 supplies previously absent Appendices A–B with evaluation prompts, resolution and output limits, baseline implementation details, training-data composition, optimizer settings, KL weight, DeepSpeed configurations and SFT hardware. It also adds code and model links. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work discussion are unchanged. Appendix citations reuse existing references without materially revising novelty or positioning against prior research.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains almost verbatim. v2 adds ethics and reproducibility statements, organized appendices and an LLM-use disclosure, updates the publication header, and repairs the unresolved appendix reference.

P2.justification: v1 Figures 1–2 are combined and redrawn as a two-panel Figure 1 with explicit policy-model and input-group labels. v2 also adds Table 4 and clarifies Table 1's frame-column caption. The remaining result displays are essentially retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v1 repeatedly directs readers to absent appendices for essential experimental details. v2 supplies prompts, preprocessing and training settings, comparator implementations and resource links, substantially reducing this reproducibility gap. Its long-video discussion also improves interpretation. These are substantial reporting gains despite unchanged accuracy evidence and residual ambiguity about the revised teacher-branch diagram.
